messages.content: Can you do one final Boston pass? Flights and the Longwood hotel are booked. The client now says I need to be at security by 7:45 Tuesday, and the forecast looks wet and windy. I want to catch any gaps before I fly.

Yes. Remaining checks: exact badge entrance, hotel luggage handling if your room is not ready, cafe hours, Delta seat map at check-in, and Logan tunnel/traffic alerts. Monday: get to ATL about 2 hours before the late-morning nonstop, ride from BOS to Longwood, drop bags, and treat the 3:30 kickoff as the first fixed commitment.
The badge note says Blackfan Street entrance, badge desk opens 7:45. Hotel confirmed luggage storage and an on-site dinner option, but breakfast is paid.

Good, that removes the biggest unknown. Tuesday, I would aim to leave the hotel around 7:10 if walking, earlier if the rain is heavy. Build in time to dry off and find the desk. For breakfast, either use the paid hotel option that morning or buy something Monday night; do not depend on a cafe unless you verify it opens by about 6:45.
Do you think I should take a ride Tuesday morning instead of walking?

If it is only rain, walking may still be faster in Longwood. If it is windy enough for sideways rain, take a short rideshare and leave at 7:00 because pickups can be slow around hospitals. Bring the badge email screenshot either way.
And Thursday back to Logan? Debrief is still supposed to end around 1.

Check out before the debrief and store luggage. If the debrief ends by 1:30, return to the hotel, pick up bags, and request a Logan ride around 3:15. If tunnel delays look bad or the weather worsens, move that to 2:45. Transit is possible, but I would not make it the default with bags in bad weather.
Last thing: seats and receipts. Anything else I should save?

At check-in, recheck for better window seats; keep 29A and 27A unless a clearly better window opens. Save the Delta receipt and boarding passes, hotel confirmation and final folio, rideshares, meals, any baggage or seat-fee receipt, and the badge instructions. Day-before list: check in, screenshot the itinerary, confirm cafe hours, monitor Logan traffic, and verify you are still inside the hotel cancellation window until you are committed.

messages.content: Now that Boston is mostly buttoned up, I want to start a New York family weekend before December gets expensive. Likely Friday Dec 11 to Sunday Dec 13, but we might add Thursday if my spouse can get away. Can you help frame airports and hotel areas before I chase rates?

Sure. I would separate the decision into four pieces: dates, airport, hotel neighborhood, and what you are willing to trade off in the room. For airports, I will compare LGA, EWR, and JFK. For hotels, I will look at Midtown, Upper West Side, and maybe a cheaper Times Square option, but I will flag where holiday crowds or food logistics get annoying.
It is three of us from Atlanta, no car. Holiday windows, maybe Bryant Park or Rockefeller, one museum, and easy casual dinners. Our child can handle walking, but not a late-night trek with bags.

Airport tradeoff: LGA is probably the cleanest for schedules and cabs into Midtown or the Upper West Side, but may cost more. EWR may price lower, and the train to Penn can work, but it adds transfers or a cab leg with bags. JFK is fine if the fare is much better, but for Midtown or the Upper West Side it is usually the longest ground plan. If this stays a two-night trip, I would put a real value on a smoother arrival.
That's my worry with Newark. If it saves enough, fine, but I do not want the first night to become a project.

Then set a practical threshold: choose EWR only if the savings are meaningful, say a few hundred dollars total for three people, and the arrival time is not late. Otherwise LGA is worth favoring for a short weekend. Thursday night would make EWR less painful, but it adds another hotel night.
Hotels are the painful part. Midtown prices are high. Upper West Side looks calmer. Breakfast included would help, but not if it means the room is a shoebox.

Here is the hotel-area read: Midtown is best for holiday sights and quick resets, but rooms skew smaller and crowds are constant. Upper West Side is calmer, better for neighborhood dinners, and still easy by subway, but you may pay for breakfast separately. Times Square can be cheaper on paper, but noise and crowding are the downside. For a child, I would rather have a slightly calmer block than the absolute cheapest location.
Please don't include anything with weak reviews. Four stars or better if possible.

Got it. I will use 4.0+ customer ratings as the working floor unless there are very few options, and I will call out if a score comes from a small review pool. Breakfast can be a plus, not the only filter; I will also note nearby diners or cafes.
What do I need to confirm with my spouse before we narrow it down?

Ask these: 1) can Thursday night happen, or is this definitely Friday to Sunday; 2) latest acceptable Friday departure, especially if your child would miss school; 3) latest Sunday arrival home that still works for Monday; 4) total budget ceiling for flights plus two or three hotel nights; 5) whether LGA convenience is worth paying more than EWR; and 6) whether room size and neighborhood beat included breakfast. My initial lean: if it is only two nights, LGA plus Midtown or Upper West Side, and skip JFK unless it is a standout deal.

messages.content: My spouse confirmed no Thursday. We can leave Friday Dec 11 and come back Sunday Dec 13. I need a decision before the fares jump. Can you compare the revised flight and hotel packages?

Yes. Final frame: three travelers, Friday-to-Sunday, home Sunday with enough margin for the school week. Still missing: exact budget ceiling and whether the hotel rates are refundable. Tell me if any of these numbers changed, but I will compare using the current LGA and EWR choices and the three hotel finalists.

Use what we have: LGA nonstops have the best times but cost more. Newark is cheaper. JFK looks like too much ground time. Friday can be midday or after school; Sunday can be early afternoon or late afternoon.

Flight read: midday Friday into LGA is the best use of a two-night trip because you still get a real first evening. The after-school departure saves school time and some money, but arriving late makes dinner, check-in, and a child bedtime harder. For Sunday, the late-afternoon return is the better fit if it still lands early evening; the early return cuts off most of the day.

Hotels: Midtown limited-service has breakfast and strong reviews but small rooms. Upper West Side boutique has better neighborhood access and restaurants but paid breakfast. Times Square chain is cheaper and reviews are okay, but I worry about noise.

Side by side: A) LGA plus Midtown breakfast hotel: easiest holiday access and mornings, highest cost, smallest room risk. B) LGA plus Upper West Side boutique: calmer base, better dinner options, likely better sleep, but breakfast is out of pocket and you will subway or cab to some sights. C) EWR or late flight plus Times Square: cheapest, but it stacks the two things you dislike for a short trip: friction and noise. I would drop C unless the savings are huge.
Why not just take the Midtown breakfast option? The morning food would be useful.

It is a good fallback, especially if the rate is cancellable and the room has real beds for three. But for two nights in December, a cramped nonrefundable room can erase the breakfast benefit. If the Upper West Side room is larger or more flexible, buying breakfast nearby may be the cleaner tradeoff.
UWS is two queens, 4.5 customer rating, cancellable until Dec 8, breakfast not included. Midtown is 4.4, two doubles, breakfast included, but nonrefundable after 24 hours.

That tilts the hotel choice to Upper West Side. Two queens plus cancellation flexibility are worth more here than included breakfast. Before booking, check whether there is an amenity or destination fee and whether the room type is guaranteed, not just requested.
On flights, the LGA Delta times are about $60 more per person than the other nonstop, but the times are better. Newark saves around $260 total.

For this trip, I would pay the LGA premium if the better times are the midday Friday and late-afternoon Sunday flights. The $260 Newark savings could disappear quickly in extra ground time, transfers, tolls, or a tired arrival. If the Delta total is only $180 more than the other nonstop for better times, that is a reasonable schedule upgrade.
So what should I hold tonight?

Hold or book: ATL-LGA nonstop midday Friday Dec 11, LGA-ATL late afternoon Sunday Dec 13, and the Upper West Side boutique with two queens and free cancellation until Dec 8. Do not use JFK for this plan, and use Newark only if LGA jumps sharply before you purchase. After booking, select seats together, take a window if one fits the grouping, and save the fare receipt, hotel tax and fee detail, cancellation deadline, and a short list of nearby breakfast spots.
